structure: layout A (64-partition, no copy): one affine_range(S//W) over the free axis, W=2048 (S/W=128 iters, power-of-two divisor -> mask-free); per tile 4 loads (x0=x_in[0:64], x1=x_in[64:128] each loaded into its OWN base-0 [64,W] tile so both tensor_tensor operands share partition base 0 with NO nl.copy realign; cos, sin) + 6 nisa.tensor_tensor (x0*cos, x1*sin, out0=sub; x0*sin, x1*cos, out1=add) + 2 stores (out0->rows 0:64 stored early to free temps; out1->rows 64:128 via partition-offset store)
notes: First correct fp32 kernel (phase 1). Path layout_a_no_copy: the no-copy partition-offset load/store form compiled+passed under --disable-dge --logical-nc-config=1, so the copy-realign fallback was not needed. rel-L2 = 0.0 exact on all 5 seeds (exact fp32 arithmetic, no approximation). HBM traffic at the read-once/write-once floor exactly (268.44MB rd + 134.22MB wr = 402.65MB = theoretical payload, AC-2 satisfied to the byte). VERDICT: vector-bound. Read together: Vec=92% near-saturated on the six tensor_tensor passes; HBM at floor (no traffic to remove); effBW~427GB/s and MBU=30% are well below the ~781GB/s silu streaming roofline, so DMA-active 94% is issue/wait busy, NOT bandwidth-bound (pure-DMA ceiling at 781GB/s = 0.516ms vs measured 0.944ms; the ~0.43ms gap is unhidden vector time). Phase-2 lever = layout B (pack both halves onto 128 partitions, 3 ops do the work of 6, ~halving vector time) WITHOUT raising HBM traffic (cos/sin via SBUF partition broadcast, not a 2nd HBM read). Finer-W is a secondary/phase-3 lever (only harvests a DMA bubble; DMA is not the dominant limiter here). Theoretical vector cost model (1.64-3.28ms) over-predicts real trn2 fp32 vector throughput (exceeds the 1.1418ms baseline doing the same 6 ops) -> measured digest is the source of truth, not the cost model. 1.209x over the 1.1418ms baseline.

structure: Layout B (128-partition packed): affine_range(S//W) W=2048 (S/W=128 iters, mask-free). Per tile: 1 natural [128,W] load A=[x0;x1]; cos/sin loaded into top half [0:64] then broadcast to [64:128] via nisa.activation(op=nl.copy,scale=1) on Scalar; x_swap_neg=[-x1;+x0] built as two cross-half nisa.activation copies on Scalar (top scale=-1 exact negate, bottom scale=1); 3 nisa.tensor_tensor over [128,W] (M1=A*cos_pack, M2=x_swap_neg*sin_pack, out=M1+M2); single [128,W] store. Sign baked into x_swap_neg so final combine is one 128-part add (AC-3). Cross-half moves legal for <=64-part ops; DGE off so no SBUF->SBUF DMA used.
notes: D1b exact all-Scalar layout B. AC-4 MATERIALIZED: Vec-active 0.865->0.429ms (~2x, the 6->3 tensor_tensor halving) AND latency fell 0.9445->0.7801ms, HBM at floor -> the packing win did not merely relocate. Build hid on the idle Scalar engine (Scl-active 0.500ms < DMA-active 0.738ms, so Scl did NOT become the critical engine). New limiter DMA-active (0.738ms, top engine); DMA-active actually DROPPED from 0.883ms at identical HBM bytes because the natural single [128,W] x-load issues cheaper than layout A's two [64,W] x-loads. RoPE moved VECTOR-BOUND -> DMA-co-limited. rel-L2=0.0 exact (pure data movement + IEEE fp32 sign flip; no PE, no downcast). KEEP per AC-5 (0.778 < 0.80ms); PE escalation (D1a/D1c) NOT triggered. Superseded by the W=512 finer-tile variant.

build_engine: PE(Tensor) for x_swap_neg; Scalar for cos/sin broadcasts
structure: Layout B (128-partition packed, D1c hybrid): affine_range(S//512) W=512 mask-free. Per tile: 1 natural [128,512] load A=[x0;x1]; cos_pack=[cos;cos] and sin_pack=[sin;sin] via nisa.activation(copy,scale=1) Scalar broadcast from top-half to bottom-half; x_swap_neg=[-x1;+x0] via nc_matmul(swap_t, a) = swap_t.T@a where swap_t.T=[[0,-I],[I,0]] (0/+-1 permutation) on the PE engine -> PSUM; 3 nisa.tensor_tensor over [128,512] with M1=A(SBUF)*cos_pack(SBUF) and M2=x_swap_neg(PSUM)*sin_pack(SBUF) (at most one PSUM operand per tensor_tensor); single [128,512] store. swap_const is a compiled nl.shared_constant loaded to SBUF once (128x128x4=65536B, trivial).
phase3_steering_verdict: Layout B BEAT layout A decisively (0.9445 -> 0.696 ms, 1.358x kernel-over-kernel; 1.209x -> 1.641x over baseline). The winning build-engine realization is HYBRID (D1c): PE for x_swap_neg permutation, Scalar for cos/sin broadcasts. The PE 0/+-1 permutation matmul is exact (rel-L2=0.0) and did NOT trigger the tf32 decomposition that AC-1.1 guards against (pleasantly surprised). Engine balance: PE 50% / Vec 69% / Scl 47% / DMA 99% -- all three compute engines hide under the DMA co-limiter. DMA-active (0.689ms) is now the sole wall-clock ceiling, effBW 578 GB/s = 74% of the 781 GB/s roofline. Phase 3: the only remaining lever is the DMA scheduling/bandwidth gap (MBU 40%, ~26% headroom to roofline). The compute engines are all sub-saturated and hidden; further layout or compute changes cannot help. The Scalar-only sibling (rope_v2_layoutB_scalar_w512, 0.7337ms) serves as a guaranteed fallback if a future compiler revision breaks the nc_matmul 0/+-1 exactness.
notes: PROMOTED. D1c hybrid PE+Scalar layout B. Beats the all-Scalar sibling by 5.2% repeatably (0.696 vs 0.734ms), which exceeds the DEC-1 ~3-5% noise-band threshold. The PE path's correctness risk (AC-1.1) did NOT materialize -- rel-L2=0.0 exact on all 5 seeds. HBM at floor (+65KB one-time swap_const, <0.02% above floor, within AC-2's +-10% tolerance).
